defects.note: r02 F1, r03 F1 and r06 F2 each say the band is stroked only on its upper edge, with the lower edge being only where a faint fill stops, so it reads as one line; r02 even proposes a second stroke at below_line_cutoff_y. r05 F2 targets the same band fill but about it lowering trace contrast, a different failure.

No finding addresses an instant before a non-zero first opening, or bisect_right returning -1 and indexing the last segment. r02 F1 and r06 F1 discuss the within-run bound refusal but about the last column overshooting stop_s, a different (upper-bound) failure.
Both say add_run checks only the run count and agent, so an unrelated same-agent controller is drawn as Run 2 of the case while case.branches does not hold it.

r04 F1 explicitly says that when the previously chosen instant disappears (dial moved and moved back before a step) max(restored, 0) falls back to induction. The others describe the selector defaulting to index 0 on first fill and never advancing; r05 F2 mentions max(restored,0) but not the vanished-keyframe case, so acting on these would not fix the fallback.

r05 F4 states it exactly. r02 F2, r03 F1 and r06 F1 each say the lock caption 'Reset the case to end this one' does not name which of two Reset buttons it means and that the branch's Reset does not end the comparison, which is the same fault, though their main thrust is the unconfirmed trunk reset.
No finding mentions the always-present notices container or the banner holders costing 12 px column spacing.

r01 F1, r03 F3 and r06 F2 say case_restarted is connected even with no case, so Reset on run 1 of a loose-controller dashboard removes the other runs. r05 F3 is about the same handler on a case dashboard deleting the branch without confirmation, a different failure (r03 F1 and r06 F1 likewise, already counted for PL-WG73).

r03 F3 says the len(self._runs)==1 early return comes before self._fork_refusal = None so the refusal stays after a lone trunk's Reset; r05 F5 says the same (cleared only on a two-run reset, early return when trunk is alone).

No finding says one flow type can be built from another (CardiacOutput(FreshGasFlow(5.0))). r02 F3 (bool, -0.0, overflow), r03 F1 (-0.0) and r04 F1 (pickle bypass) point at the same constructors but describe different failures.

No finding addresses _require_built's incomplete swapped-type naming or {value!r} raising ValueError for huge ints. r02 F3's OverflowError from math.isfinite is in the constructors, not _require_built, so it is not counted even as a near miss.

r05 F2 finds a mark added after the crossing read differently by the halt branch and the mark branch, but it compares the two branch doors and recommends making the halt door copy _resume_point_at_mark's reconstruction, which would not fix the branch disagreeing with the trunk's recorded crossings; near miss. r01 F1, r02 F1, r04 F1 and r05 F1 target _resume_point_at_mark but are about a setting changed at the fork instant being already applied.

r01 F2 says the rollback catches only Exception, so a BaseException such as KeyboardInterrupt leaves a half-applied step, which is the key defect. r02 F2, r03 F1 and r04 F2 point at the same rollback clauses in advance() but describe a different failure: the rollback restoring the validator after an accounting failure, or the error message quoting rolled-back totals.

r02 F2 says SimulationState.__post_init__ does not check the run length, so a state with step_count=10_000_000 builds and reports an elapsed time past the cap until the next advance() refuses it. It recommends the check in __post_init__, which is exactly the key defect and its fix.

No finding says that a run standing exactly on 86 400 s before any step is refused reads Paused, offers Start and shows no limit notice because only the latch records the limit. r01 F4 and r05 F2 discuss the controller path that sets supported_limit_reason, but their concern is missing integration tests, a different failure.

No finding mentions a failed run's outstanding marks reading 'still running'. The listed findings point at the same standings code (BookmarkSet.standings or _time_bookmark_standing) but describe time marks at or before the clock, a different input and cause. r04 F2, that standings() is not given the run's state, is the closest.

Each of these findings explicitly names a time bookmark at the run's opening instant (0 s on a trunk, or a branch's fork instant). Each explains that crossed_between is open at the step start while the BEFORE_THIS_BRANCH test is strict, so the mark reads STILL_RUNNING for good. Some also widen the case to marks already behind the clock, but fixing what they describe fixes the key defect.

Each says _refresh_bookmarks draws the standings of snapshots[0] alone, so with several runs the panel shows one run's reached or not-reached answer as the whole case's. That is the key defect. r04 has no such finding.

The same findings say that a second run or branch that halts on its own crossing shows no 'reached' row, because only the reference run's standings are drawn. r01 F4 says the row stays blank for the mark the second run stopped on. r02 F3 says the row stays blank. r03 F4 says a halt on run B never shows. r05 F4 says the panel says nothing. r06 F4 says a mark reached by a second run shows no standing and the trunk comes first. The cause and the fix are the same as for the key.

r01 F2 and r05 F1 both say that pickle protocols 0 and 1 rebuild SimulationStep through copyreg._reconstructor and float.__new__, which skips the range check, and both propose a __reduce__ to fix it. That is the counted part exactly. r05 F2 is about the same SimulationStep.__new__ code but describes a check-versus-stored-value mismatch for Decimal and Fraction inputs, a different failure.

r05 F1 says LayoutModel.split refuses a part only when its size is exactly zero, so it can create an Area narrower than BORDER_ALIGNMENT_TOLERANCE whose edges borders() treats as one line. It asks split to refuse such cuts, which fixes the key's cause. r01 F1 describes the same tolerance-sliver behaviour but is anchored on resize/_moved and proposes refusing or clamping drags. It mentions split with a small cut only in passing, so acting on its fix would not change split, and it is recorded as a close-call near miss.

r06 F1 says that at 300x each 0.1 s tick is 30 simulated seconds, so control changes land only at tick boundaries and the same gesture gives a different run at each rate, contradicting the claim that faster playback is not a modelling change. That is the same fault and the same cause as the key's uninterruptible burst. The tick-drift findings point at the same loop but describe the achieved rate falling below the displayed rate, which is a different failure.

No finding mentions round() on an infinite quotient or an OverflowError for a tiny step. Several findings note that steps_per_tick is called outside the try, so its intended refusal escapes the loop. That is the right function but a different failure: the caught refusal, not the bare overflow inside the conversion.

No finding addresses resumed_at's whole-object settings comparison, its fixed message that blames the timeline, or the uncompared agent MAC, display name and vaporizer maximum. The findings about reset, set_agent on a branch, the frame of run_segments and float-instant refusal in _resume_point_at describe other faults in other code paths, so none is even a near miss.

Each counted finding says that _resume_point_at (resumed_at) passes crossing=None at a keyframe where the trunk stands halted, so the branch disagrees with the trunk and with the halt-door branch, as still_running against reached or before_this_branch against passed. Seeding the halt's crossing, which is the fix they propose, is the key's case 3. r02 F2 is the time-mark form of the same cause. r06 F1 and r01 F3 describe the same symptom of a time mark at a control-event fork but attribute it to exact float comparison in _time_bookmark_standing. Acting on them (a tolerance) would not fix the missing crossing or the MAC-target case.

All three say that CaseInstant.__new__ checks only the value, so CaseInstant(StepCount(...)) builds an instant, while require_case_instant refuses that swap. All three propose refusing the checked quantities in __new__, which is exactly the key's defect.

No finding says that the record column's stretch weighting takes about 306 px instead of the ratified 228 px sidebar width, leaving the readout row on four columns at 1366 px. The Ignored-vertical-policy findings point at _build_unconditional_region but describe vertical clipping of the record. r01 F2 discusses horizontal width allocation between the readout and record columns, but its failure is the record being clipped in a narrower window, not the readouts wrapping.

r04 F4 names the same mechanism: after the shift, a zero-rate state's diagonal entry is a few ulps off 1, and the 2^s squarings amplify that into a silently wrong propagator. It asks for a bound or refusal on interval times norm, which is the missing cap. Its example decays the entry instead of growing it, but the cause is the same. r01 F1 (fixed point a few ulps off F_D) and r05 F2 / r03 F1 (rows summing above 1, fraction above 1) are rounding faults in the same propagator with different failures.

r03 F3 names the _squarings_for overflow: ceil(log2(inf)) raises a bare OverflowError instead of SimulationConfigurationError, and it proposes a finiteness check on the quotient. r04 F4 names the same OverflowError and also a wrong (zeroed) result that is returned silently. Both name the overflow half of the key; neither describes the all-zero propagator with accounting passing more exactly than that.

Each finding says the direct sigMouseMoved slot reads the position that the SignalProxy timer stored for the previous event, so the current move is answered for a stale position, or not answered at all.
Each finding says nothing clears the stored pointer position on leave, so the hover box stays up and keeps refreshing for a pointer that has gone.
No finding mentions the hover box flip threshold or its clipping on the 200 px wash-in plot.
No finding addresses nearest_trace_point choosing one nearest point across several runs.
No finding says the hover line fails to name the run on a frame that holds several runs.

The instant-rounding findings (r03 F4, r04 F2, r05 F4, r06 F2) concern HOVER_INSTANT_RESOLUTION_S in _hover_context, not the two-dimensional _pixel_distance column choice, so they are not counted and are not near misses at this code.

No finding names the missing type test (True admitted as 1.0 s, a huge int raising OverflowError). r01 F1, r02 F2 and r06 F1 point at require_supported_case_instant but describe a disagreement with the step-count guard at overshoot steps. r02 F3 and r06 F2 describe OverflowError and ValueError in require_supported_step_count, a different guard with a different cause, so they are not counted.
r03 F1 says Fraction and Percent refuse only each other and silently accept the other checked float types, citing Fraction(SimulationStep(0.05)). That is exactly the key's defect.

Each finding says _settle reads a View's need only on build, show, resize or drag, never after refresh draws the Views, so frames stay pinned at a stale need. The findings reach it through a branch adding a run rather than the first frame. Re-settling after refresh fixes the same cause, including the late re-settle jump at launch width.

Same fault as the key: refresh draws Views that add per-run widgets without settling again, so the Areas and the page keep the earlier need. The findings use a second run, not the first frame, as the trigger, which counts as a slightly different input with the same cause.

All six findings say minimumSizeHint returns the cached _least after the Views' needs grow, so the scrolling page does not grow. r02 F4, r03 F2, r05 F3 and r06 F3 point at the same _least / minimum_extent computation but describe a different fault: it uses needs instead of the larger of need and floor.
